title: Jackson Square Aviation selects RTX's Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engine to power Airbus A320neo aircraft
summary: LONDON, July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Air show – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today that Jackson Square Aviation (JSA), a global leader in aviation leasing, has selected the GTF engine to power an undisclosed number of Airbus A320neo family aircraft.
body_text: Jackson Square Aviation selects RTX's Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engine to power Airbus A320neo aircraft July 20, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email LONDON , July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Air show – Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today that Jackson Square Aviation (JSA), a global leader in aviation leasing, has selected the GTF engine to power an undisclosed number of Airbus A320neo family aircraft. "This order underscores continued confidence in the GTF engine as we continue to build on our long-standing relationship with JSA to support the growing fleet of A320neo operators worldwide," said Rick Deurloo, president of Commercial Engines, Pratt & Whitney. "GTF engines have been instrumental to our growth strategy for fleet and customer base expansion," said Kevin McDonald, CEO of Jackson Square Aviation. "The unmatched fuel efficiency and noise reduction are a game changer for A320neo operators." JSA's portfolio currently includes 91 GTF-powered A320neo family aircraft and 11 V2500-powered A320ceos. The GTF delivers 20% lower fuel consumption and a 75% smaller noise footprint compared to the prior generation of engines. Over 2,800 GTF-powered aircraft are operated globally by more than 90 customers, and the order backlog of over 8,000 GTF engines reflects strong market demand for its proven benefits. The engine's revolutionary geared architecture is the right foundation for next generation technologies. About Jackson Square Aviation Jackson Square Aviation is a global commercial aircraft lessor focused on providing airlines with reliable, long-term fleet and financing solutions. We work in close partnership with our customers, combining a deep understanding of their operational priorities with a consistent and pragmatic approach to capital deployment. Our business is anchored in operating lease products, complemented by targeted financing solutions that support airline fleet replacement and growth. Through our relationships with manufacturers, financiers, and industry partners, we provide the flexibility and certainty airlines require in a dynamic market. Since our founding in 2010, JSA has built a portfolio of modern, fuel-efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft. Today, our owned, committed, and managed fleet totals 344 aircraft, serving 64 airlines across 34 countries. Our approach is guided by a clear set of values: integrity in how we operate, collaboration in how we work, and a commitment to continuous improvement. We remain focused on building a resilient, high-quality platform that supports our customers and positions the business for long-term success. Jackson Square Aviation is part of the Mitsubishi HC Capital group, a global leasing company based in Japan and publicly listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. About Pratt & Whitney Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, RTX pushes the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact [email protected] . title: Fraudulent Transactions: How to Identify and Prevent Them
summary: Learn what a fraudulent transaction is, common fraud types, warning signs, detection methods, and tips to protect your payments.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle Every day, thousands of digital payment fraud attempts target consumers and businesses. From phishing scams and fake UPI requests to account takeovers and card-not-present fraud, online payment fraud continues to evolve. Understanding how fraudulent transactions happen – and how to identify them early – can help prevent financial loss and protect customer trust. What is a Fraudulent Transaction? A fraudulent transaction is any payment or account activity carried out without the cardholder’s or account owner’s authorization. It usually occurs when fraudsters steal or misuse sensitive information such as card details, banking credentials, passwords, or OTPs to make purchases, transfer funds, or access accounts without the user’s knowledge. Types of Fraudulent Transactions Online payment fraud can take many forms. Here are some of the most common types businesses and consumers encounter. Card-Not-Present (CNP) Fraud This occurs when a card is used for online or phone purchases without being physically presented. Since merchants cannot verify the physical card, fraudsters often exploit stolen card details to complete unauthorized transactions. Account Takeover (ATO) Fraud Fraudsters gain access to a customer’s online banking or payment account using stolen credentials. Once inside, they can transfer money, change account details, or make unauthorized purchases. Phishing Scams Scammers impersonate banks or trusted organizations through emails, SMS, or calls to trick users into revealing passwords, OTPs, or banking information. Fake UPI Payment Requests Fraudsters send fake payment or collect requests disguised as legitimate transactions. Approving these requests can result in unauthorized money transfers from the victim’s account. Also read: Fake UPI Payment App Scams: Spot Fake PhonePe APKs & GPay Apps Merchant Fraud Fraudsters create fake online stores or merchant identities to collect payments without delivering genuine products or services. How to Identify a Fraudulent Transaction Fraudulent transactions are easier to stop when detected early. Watch for these warning signs: Payments you don’t recognize Multiple small transactions within a short period Transactions from unusual locations or at odd hours International payments you didn’t authorize Duplicate charges for the same purchase Charges from unfamiliar merchants OTP requests you didn’t initiate Not every unusual transaction is fraudulent. It could be a recurring subscription, a family member’s purchase, or a merchant using a different billing name. If anything seems suspicious, verify it immediately with your bank or payment provider. Also read: Fake Payment Screenshot Scams: How to Identify & Prevent UPI Fraud How Fraudulent Transactions Are Detected Banks and payment providers use multiple security measures to detect suspicious activity before it causes financial loss. Common fraud detection methods include: Transaction pattern analysis Velocity checks for repeated transactions Device and IP monitoring OTP and multi-factor authentication verification Risk scoring and blacklist checks Behavioral analysis to identify unusual user activity Businesses also monitor unusually large orders, repeated payment failures, billing and shipping mismatches, and abnormal customer behavior to identify potential fraud early. What to Do If You Discover a Fraudulent Transaction If you discover that a payment transaction was made without your knowledge or consent, take action now. Check your banking institution or mobile banking application to verify the exact dollar amount, date/time and transaction ID associated with the disputed transaction(s). Block your credit/debit card, digital wallet or account if necessary. Contact your banking institution/ payment processor immediately. Report the disputed transaction as unauthorized to your banking institution/payment processor. Save copies/screenshots of SMS/Email notifications confirming the dispute along with any documentation supporting your claim. Change passwords/PIN numbers on accounts that may have been compromised by an unauthorized party. File a Cyber Crime Complaint via your Country’s Official Reporting Process (if required). Prompt Action is Important Because Banking Institutions and Payment Networks May Be Able to Freeze or Track a Disputed Transaction Based Upon Timely Notification From the Account Holder. Suspicious Transaction vs. Fraudulent Transaction Although the terms are often used interchangeably, they are different. Suspicious Transaction Fraudulent Transaction Appears unusual or unexpected Confirmed unauthorized activity Requires verification Requires immediate action May be legitimate Involves deception or unauthorized access For example, a forgotten subscription renewal is suspicious until verified, whereas a payment made using stolen credentials is fraudulent. Why Do Fraudulent Transactions Occur? Most payment fraud happens because fraudsters gain access to sensitive information through: Phishing emails/fake support calls designed to obtain sensitive account information. Stolen account numbers/card details. Weak passwords/password reuse. Malicious QR code or fake payment pages used to steal sensitive account information. Malware installed on devices (phones/computers). Social Engineering tactics where victims are tricked into providing their sensitive information to scammers posing as representatives of banks/institutions. Most fraud cases do not require sophisticated hacking techniques. They rely on unsuspecting victims being hurried/distracted/convinced to provide sensitive information. How Businesses Can Prevent Transaction Fraud Since businesses suffer losses related to revenue, chargebacks , and customer distrust as a result of fraudulent transactions, they can implement various measures to mitigate these risks. These include: Setting transaction limits Using fraud detection and risk-scoring tools Reviewing high-value or high-risk orders Monitoring repeated payment failures Securing checkout with two-factor authentication Tracking refund and chargeback patterns Preventing fraud does not solely involve preventing malicious activities. It is equally important to minimize false positives and allow legitimate customers to continue processing transactions successfully. How Individuals Can Reduce Fraud Risk Individuals can lower their exposure to fraudulent transactions by implementing a few basic habits. This includes: Never share OTPs, UPI PINs, or passwords. Use strong, unique passwords. Enable transaction alerts. Review bank statements regularly. Avoid clicking suspicious links. Verify website URLs before making payments. Lock cards when they are not in use, if supported by your bank. Staying alert and following basic security practices can prevent many common fraud attempts. How Cashfree Payments Helps Businesses Cashfree Payments helps businesses reduce payment fraud through a combination of secure payment infrastructure and RiskShield , its AI-powered fraud prevention engine. RiskShield uses real-time risk scoring, behavioral analysis, device intelligence, and customizable fraud rules to detect suspicious transactions before they impact your business . Along with transaction monitoring and payment tracking, it enables businesses to reduce fraud losses, minimize false positives, and provide customers with a secure checkout experience. Final Thoughts Fraudulent transactions can impact both individuals and businesses, but early detection and quick action can significantly reduce financial losses. Understanding common fraud types, recognizing warning signs, and following secure payment practices are key to protecting your money and maintaining customer trust in today’s digital payment ecosystem. FAQs What is a fraudulent transaction? A fraudulent transaction is any payment or account activity made without the cardholder’s or account owner’s permission. It usually involves stolen payment information, compromised accounts, or deceptive tactics such as phishing and fake payment requests. How do I detect fraudulent transactions? Fraudulent transaction detection refers to the identification of questionable or unauthorized payments prior to them causing further damage. How can I tell if a transaction was fraudulent? Use your judgment! If you don’t recognize the payment, did not authorize it or are seeing unusual activity in your account, consider it suspect and contact your bank immediately. Can a fraudulent transaction be reversed? Possibly yes, depending on when you report it and the payment method used. The more quickly you act, the better. Is a suspicious transaction the same as fraud? No. A suspicious transaction is one that is unusual; however, a fraudulent transaction represents proven unauthorized activity. What should I do first if I discover a fraudulent transaction? Block the payment method from further use if possible. Call your bank, credit union or payment provider immediately. Can businesses automatically detect fraudulent transactions? Yes. Most businesses utilize some form of fraud scoring, behavior analysis, velocity checks and other tools to identify potential fraud immediately. Why are there so many fraudulent transactions? Because thieves have stolen information using phishing methods, account takeovers and social engineering tactics to trick people or bypass security measures. How do I prevent fraudulent transactions? Follow safe practices: keep passwords secure, never give out one-time passcodes (OTPs), and check your statements regularly. title: AudioCodes Unveils AI-First Intelligent Meeting Room
summary: AudioCodes, a leading provider of voice, contact center, and conversational AI applications and services for enterprises, today announced the launch of the AudioCodes Intelligent Meeting Room, an innovative solution that leverages artificial intelligence (AI) technology to transform the hybrid meeting experience.
body_text: AI-powered meeting summaries and smart video enhance collaboration and overall organizational productivity Or Yehuda, Israel – January 13, 2025 - AudioCodes (NASDAQ: AUDC) Press Release AudioCodes, a leading provider of voice, contact center, and conversational AI applications and services for enterprises, today announced the launch of the AudioCodes Intelligent Meeting Room , an innovative solution that leverages artificial intelligence (AI) technology to transform the hybrid meeting experience. The solution integrates cutting-edge conversational AI-generated meeting summarization and intelligent video capabilities into AudioCodes’ RXV series of meeting room devices to boost hybrid meeting productivity and ensure an immersive experience for all participants, whether they are located on-site or remotely. The Intelligent Meeting Room’s automatic summarization uses generative AI integrated with AudioCodes’ room devices to create and share summaries, enabling in-room participants to focus on the ongoing discussions rather than on manual note-taking. This capability is activated easily with a click via the RX-PAD meeting controller console. Powered by Meeting Insights , AudioCodes’ award-winning technology, this functionality transforms online meeting content into a valuable corporate knowledge repository. The solution also includes advanced visual AI capabilities built into the RXV series devices and cameras, including face detection and speaker tracking. It leverages multiple camera streams to provide a comprehensive view of both individual participants and the entire room, fostering powerful meeting equity and delivering an immersive experience for remote attendees. “A critical element of today’s complex business reality is the ability to conduct effective hybrid meetings and quickly act on their outcomes," said Nati Davidi, VP of IP Phone Solutions and Devices Business Line at AudioCodes. "Our Intelligent Meeting Room solution addresses these issues head-on by integrating advanced AI capabilities for automatic meeting summaries and intelligent video. This not only enhances the overall experience but also fosters meeting equity, ensuring that both on-site and remote participants can engage fully and effectively, ultimately driving productivity and innovation.” AudioCodes will be demonstrating the Intelligent Meeting Room solution at ISE 2025 in Barcelona on February 4-7, 2025. Come and meet the AudioCodes’ teams at booth 1D170 or click here to book a meeting.

title: Closing Industrial Wastewater Data Gaps with Flow, Water Quality & Gas Monitoring
summary: Integrated monitoring technologies help industrial operators understand wastewater quantity, quality and safety conditions across treatment processes.
body_text: The Three Pillars of Reliable Wastewater Monitoring Effective industrial wastewater management relies on three core monitoring disciplines: flow measurement, water quality monitoring and gas detection. Together, they provide the visibility needed to support compliance, safety and operational performance. Flow Measurement Flow measurement provides the foundation for compliance reporting, billing and process optimization by accurately tracking discharge volumes throughout wastewater treatment systems. Depending on the application, operators may use electromagnetic or ultrasonic flow measurement technologies to monitor wastewater movement and verify discharge volumes. Solutions such as the ModMAG® M2000 and Dynasonics® TFX-5000 support reliable measurement across a wide range of industrial wastewater environments. Water Quality Monitoring Continuous water quality monitoring helps operators identify process changes, reduce compliance risks and better understand treatment performance across industrial wastewater applications. Monitoring stations, spectrometer probes and physical sensors can provide visibility into key parameters such as pH, COD, BOD, turbidity, temperature, dissolved oxygen and total suspended solids (TSS). Technologies such as the Q-Series , spectro::lyser V3 and con::cube V3 help deliver real-time insight into changing wastewater conditions and treatment performance. Gas Detection Gas detection helps protect personnel and assets by identifying hazardous gas conditions early, supporting worker safety, maintenance activities and regulatory compliance. Depending on facility requirements, operators may use fixed, portable or area-monitoring technologies to detect toxic and combustible gases such as H₂S, methane and VOCs. Solutions such as the F12D Toxic Gas Detector and D12 Toxic and Combustible Gas Detector provide continuous monitoring to support safer wastewater operations.

title: FMC Corporation Announces Agreement to Divest India Commercial Business to Crystal Crop Protection Limited
summary: FMC Corporation (NYSE:FMC), a leading global agricultural sciences company, announced today it has signed a definitive agreement to sell FMC India Private Limited (FMC India) to Crystal Crop Protection Limited, a crop solutions company in India, for consideration of $252 million USD, subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt and working capital.
body_text: FMC Corporation (NYSE:FMC), a leading global agricultural sciences company, announced today it has signed a definitive agreement to sell FMC India Private Limited (FMC India) to Crystal Crop Protection Limited, a crop solutions company in India, for consideration of $252 million USD, subject to customary adjustments for cash, debt and working capital. FMC will continue to receive all cash generated from the ongoing operation of the India business until closing, primarily through monetization of working capital. In July 2025, FMC announced its decision to divest the company’s crop protection commercial business in India, enabling FMC to participate in the Indian market through a new go-to-market approach while deploying resources to its highest-growth opportunities globally. The transaction is expected to close by year-end 2026, subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions. FMC intends to allocate all proceeds from the sale to debt reduction. “Crystal Crop Protection Limited is well-positioned to serve Indian farmers with FMC’s portfolio of innovative technologies, and we look forward to supporting their growth through our supply agreement,” said Pierre Brondeau, FMC chairman, chief executive officer and president. “FMC remains committed to India and will continue to conduct global R&D activities and maintain global manufacturing operations in the country .” Through this transaction, Crystal Crop Protection Limited will acquire FMC India's commercial operations in the crop protection field, including a license to FMC's brands sold in India. Crystal Crop Protection Limited will also receive a preferred supply agreement for certain FMC active ingredients and formulated products, as well as preferred access to FMC's pipeline of active ingredients in India for the crop protection field. "We are excited on signing this definitive agreement to acquire this business of FMC in India,” said Ankur Aggarwal, chairman and managing director, Crystal Crop Protection Limited. “We look forward to welcoming a talented workforce into the Crystal group and aim at accelerating innovation across both chemical and biological domains of crop protection. FMC’s innovative portfolio, blockbuster brands and future pipeline give us an opportunity to provide Indian farmers access to innovative products. We look forward to further enhancing and building on our relationship with FMC.” BofA Securities acted as exclusive financial adviser while Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP served as U.S. legal adviser and Khaitan & Co assisted as legal adviser for FMC on this transaction. EY acted as exclusive buy side M&A adviser to Crystal Crop Protection Limited and Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co served as legal adviser. Further terms and conditions of the agreement were not disclosed. About FMC FMC Corporation is a global agricultural sciences company dedicated to helping growers produce food, feed, fiber and fuel for an expanding world population while adapting to a changing environment. FMC's innovative crop protection solutions – including biologicals, crop nutrition, digital and precision agriculture – enable growers and crop advisers to address their toughest challenges economically while protecting the environment. FMC is committed to discovering new herbicide, insecticide and fungicide active ingredients, product formulations and pioneering technologies that are consistently better for the planet. Visit fmc.com to learn more and follow us on LinkedIn ® . About Crystal Crop Protection Limited Established in 1994, Crystal Crop Protection Limited is a crop solutions company with agrochemicals and seeds at the core of its offerings. It operates on a fully integrated model, that integrates robust synthesis research and development in crop protection products and natural crop solutions as well as robust seeds breeding program, with backward-integrated technology enabled manufacturing and pan-India distribution, with a farmer-centric approach. title: We Put a 27B Model in Your Pocket: PrismML Bonsai 1-bit on iPhone, Android, and Mac
summary: Run a 27 billion parameter LLM on your phone. PrismML's 1-bit Bonsai reasoning models are live in the RunAnywhere apps on iOS, Android, and macOS, including the first true 1-bit model ever to run on any NPU.
body_text: Two years ago, a 27 billion parameter model was a data center tenant. It wanted a workstation GPU, 54 GB of memory, and a power supply you could hear. This week we ran one on an iPhone. In a production app you can install right now. Bonsai-27B 1-bit answering on an iPhone 17 Pro, recorded on device. Nothing leaves the phone. The model is Bonsai-27B , PrismML's 1-bit rebuild of Qwen3.6 27B: same architecture, but every weight stored in a single bit. Not 4-bit, not 8-bit. One. It launched on July 14, crossed a million downloads in four days, and topped Hacker News with a 700-point thread. Almost all of those downloads went to desktops and servers. The question everyone kept asking in those threads was whether any of this actually works on a phone. It does. And on Android we went one step further, onto silicon where no 1-bit model had ever run: the NPU. Here is what that took. One bit per weight, and why that is not a typo Quantization normally works by rounding a trained model's weights to fewer bits, and below 4 bits the wheels usually come off. Bonsai is different: PrismML trains the low-bit representation directly. Every weight is +1 or -1, and one FP16 scale is shared across each group of 128 weights. Total cost: 1.125 bits per weight, embeddings and attention included, with no higher-precision escape hatches. The results read like a misprint. PrismML reports the 1-bit 27B keeps about 90 percent of the FP16 model's quality, 76.11 against 85.07 on their 15-benchmark thinking-mode average. And here is the part that should not be possible: at 3.9 GB it outscores the 9.4 GB 2-bit quant of the same base model, which manages only 72.73. Smaller than the standard low-bit quant, and better. That is why we cleared our week when these weights dropped. Live on iPhone, Android, and Mac The full Bonsai family, 1.7B through 27B in both 1-bit and 2-bit ternary variants, is in the RunAnywhere apps today. All of them reason: the apps stream the model's thinking as it works. Here they are, side by side: Bonsai on Android, MacBook, and iPhone. One app, every backend. And yes, the 27B 1-bit runs on all three. On a MacBook and an iPhone it runs through MLX or llama.cpp; on Android it runs through QHexRT on the Hexagon NPU, a world first we will get to in a minute, with llama.cpp covering every other CPU on the planet. Same models, same app, pick your device. An 8B reasoning model in 1.21 GB deserves a second look. That is smaller than most photo libraries. None of this was download-and-go. Bonsai's hybrid architecture, with GatedDeltaNet linear-attention layers, and its Q1_0 weight format are so new that stock llama.cpp cannot load these files yet, and 1-bit MLX support is still an open upstream PR. We integrated PrismML's forks of both, pinned in our open SDK , so the apps just work. Then there was the part nobody had done at all. The first true 1-bit model on any NPU PrismML ships Bonsai for Apple Silicon and CUDA. On Android, the officially blessed answer is the CPU. The Hexagon NPU sitting in every modern Snapdragon, the most power-efficient inference silicon in the phone, has no idea what a binary matmul is. Its instruction set was never taught one. A few research teams have gotten ternary models, 1.58 bits per weight, running on Hexagon in proof-of-concept demos. True binary weights, +1 and -1 and nothing else, had never executed on an NPU. Not on Hexagon, not on anyone's. So we taught it. We wrote a custom QNN op package, a hand-built DSP-side binary that unpacks Bonsai's 1-bit weight groups and executes them on the Hexagon Tensor Processor. It installs alongside Qualcomm's standard skels, and QHexRT , our Hexagon runtime, routes Bonsai inference through it. The integration is public in the SDK; the compiled bundles are on our Hugging Face . Bonsai-4B reasoning on the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU. The first true 1-bit model to run on an NPU. Bonsai-4B and 8B run on Hexagon v75 and v81. The 27B runs on v81, the Snapdragon 8 Elite class. To our knowledge, RunAnywhere is the only runtime executing a true 1-bit model on any NPU today, and the only app shipping Bonsai on Android at all. This is not a lab demo. It is in the app on the Play Store, and you can run it before you finish this post. Measure it yourself Launch posts are where benchmarks go to be believed too easily, so we built the measurement into the product. The RunAnywhere apps include a benchmark harness: multi-trial runs, median with min and max variance, tokens per second, time to first token, prefill and decode split, memory delta, and a shareable results card at the end. We ran it on the big one. Bonsai-27B 1-bit on an iPhone 17 Pro, on the CPU through llama.cpp: 10 tokens per second, with time to first token around 2 seconds. For a 27 billion parameter reasoning model on a phone, we will take it. Bonsai-27B 1-bit on an iPhone 17 Pro: 10 tokens per second, 1813ms time to first token Now run it yourself. Download a Bonsai model on your phone, run the benchmark, and post the card. Share it with us on X @RunAnywhereAI and tag us. We would much rather argue about your numbers than ours, and we want to see the spread across devices. Try it The apps are free, on the App Store and Google Play . Open the model catalog, find PrismML, tap Get, and watch 27 billion parameters think on hardware you already own. Models: huggingface.co/runanywhere and huggingface.co/prism-ml SDK: github.com/RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks QHexRT: what it is and how it performs The phone in your pocket just became a reasoning machine. And if it is a Snapdragon, it is reasoning on silicon nobody had unlocked until this week. We think that is worth a download.

title: A Small Business's Guide to Finding and Working with Influencers
summary: Want to leverage the power of influencer marketing for your small business? Check out this guide for tips on identifying, reaching out to, and partnering w
body_text: In today's digital age, it's hard to find a business that isn't on social media. After all, it's become one of the most important marketing strategies out there to date. And one of the most effective ways to promote your brand on social media is through influencer marketing. In case you didn't know—though at this point, who doesn't know—influencers are individuals who have a significant following on social media and are able to, well, influence their audience's purchasing decisions. This kind of marketing strategy is often coveted by most brands because unlike traditional advertising methods, it's less "salesy"—in that influencers can often sell your product with their own authentic voices, opinions, and experiences. If you're reading this, you probably have heard about influencer marketing and are looking to get started. And you're in luck because in this article, we'll give you the most comprehensive guide to influencer marketing, especially if you're a small business owner just starting out. What is influencer marketing? First thing's first, we should take time to understand exactly what influencer marketing is. We talk about it briefly above, but influencer marketing is a type of digital marketing strategy that utilizes influencers—or people with an online presence who have the power to influence others—to promote products or services. With a large following, these individuals can help any brand or business reach potential customers and build brand awareness . Like we mention in the introduction, unlike traditional advertising, influencer marketing focuses on relationship building and trust between the influencer and their followers in order to establish a connection with potential customers. This is because they will often use tactics that are more authentic to their personal brand voice versus promote a product in the same way a brand would. Many influencers focus on delivering value to their audiences versus simply promoting products, so even the people following these influencers themselves are more likely to trust influencer recommendations , even if they know it's a sponsored post. Benefits of influencer marketing Influencer marketing can be a great way for small businesses to reach new audiences and foster relationships with their customers. Some of the key benefits of influencer marketing include: Increased brand awareness Having an influencer talk about your product or service is a great way to get in front of new audiences. Influencers can help you reach new people and expand your customer base. Cost-effectiveness Influencer marketing is often a more cost-effective way to reach potential customers than traditional advertising. You don’t have to pay for expensive campaigns when you work with influencers, making it an attractive option for small businesses on a tight budget. Authenticity People trust influencers more than traditional ads, so when they recommend your product or service, it’s seen as authentic and credible. This makes it easier to build trust with potential customers and turn them into loyal fans. Types of social media influencers Before we dive into how to start influencer marketing, let's first understand the different types of social media influencers. Influencers are typically categorized based on the size of their following. The four main categories of social media influencers are: Nano-Influencers Nano-influencers are individuals with a following of 1,000 to 10,000 on social media. They are often everyday people who have built a small but loyal following around a specific niche or interest. Nano-influencers are known for their high engagement rates and are an excellent option for small businesses with a limited budget. Micro-Influencers Micro-influencers are individuals with a following of 10,000 to 100,000 on social media. They are often experts in a particular field or niche and have built a loyal following around their expertise. Micro-influencers are known for their high engagement rates and are an excellent option for small businesses looking to target a specific audience. Macro-Influencers Macro-influencers are individuals with a following of 100,000 to 1 million on social media. They are often celebrities, athletes, or social media stars who have built a massive following around their personal brand. Macro-influencers are known for their broad reach and are an excellent option for small businesses looking to target a large audience. Mega-Influencers Mega-influencers are individuals with a following of over 1 million on social media. They are often A-list celebrities or social media stars who have built a massive following around their personal brand. Mega-influencers are known for their broad reach and are an excellent option for large businesses with a significant budget. How Much Does Social Influencer Marketing Cost? The cost of social influencer marketing varies depending on the size of the influencer's following, the type of content you want them to create, and the length of the campaign. According to a survey by Influencer Marketing Hub, the average cost per post for an influencer with 100,000 followers is $1,000. However, this cost can vary significantly depending on the influencer's niche, engagement rate, and other factors. How to Start Influencer Marketing as a Small Business Now that we have a better understanding of the different types of social media influencers and the cost of influencer marketing, let's dive into how small businesses can start influencer marketing. 1. Determine Your Goals Before you start looking for influencers, you need to determine your goals for the campaign. Do you want to increase brand awareness, drive sales, or promote a new product? Once you have a clear idea of your goals, you can start looking for influencers who align with your objectives. 2. Know Who You're Trying to Influence It's essential to know your target audience before you start looking for influencers. Who are your ideal customers, and what social media platforms do they use? Once you have a clear understanding of your target audience, you can start looking for influencers who have a similar audience. 3. Understand the Rules Before you start working with influencers, it's essential to understand the rules and regulations around influencer marketing. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requires influencers to disclose any sponsored content. Make sure you and the influencer you're working with are following these guidelines. Relevance Make sure the influencer you're working with is relevant to your brand. If you're a fitness brand, it wouldn't make sense to work with a food blogger. Make sure the influencer's niche aligns with your brand. Reach The influencer's reach is also an important factor to consider. While it's tempting to work with influencers with a massive following, it's essential to consider their engagement rate. An influencer with a smaller following but a high engagement rate may be more effective than an influencer with a massive following but a low engagement rate. How Much Does It Cost To Work With Local Influencers? Working with local influencers can be an effective way for small businesses to reach a local audience. The cost of working with local influencers varies depending on the size of their following and the type of content you want them to create. According to Proxi, the average cost per post for an Instagram influencer with 10,000 to 50,000 followers is $250 to $500. However, this cost can vary depending on the influencer's niche and engagement rate. If you're looking for more information about how to work with influencers even when you're just a small business with no budget, check out our complete guide that shows you how . Measure Your Results It's essential to measure the results of your influencer marketing campaign to determine its effectiveness. You can track metrics such as engagement rate, reach, and conversions to determine the ROI of your campaign. What are low-cost ways to work with influencers? Compensating influencers for their work doesn't always have to be expensive. Here are some low-cost ways to compensate influencers for their work: Gifting Giving away free products or services to influencers is a more cost-effective option than paying them in cash. This is a great way to build a relationship with influencers and get them to promote your brand. Performance-based pay This is a simple form of payment that is easy to track. An influencer would post recommending a product, and the brand would only pay them when their content converts a customer, or triggers a successful event like a purchase, booking, download, newsletter signup, etc. Fixed-rate + performance bonus This is a combination of a fixed payment and a performance bonus. The fixed payment is a guaranteed amount paid to the influencer, while the performance bonus is paid based on the success of the campaign. Content licensing fees This is a payment made to the influencer for the use of their content in the brand's marketing materials. Comped events Brands can offer influencers free tickets, backstage passes, or VIP access to use as influencer compensation. This is a great way to build a relationship with influencers and get them to promote your brand. Host a special event Brands can host a special event, just for influencers, as a way to compensate them for their work. This is a great way to build a relationship with influencers and get them to promote your brand. By using these low-cost ways to compensate influencers, small businesses can still run an effective influencer marketing campaign without breaking the bank. Best influencer marketing tools for small businesses There are several influencer marketing tools available that can help small businesses find and work with influencers. Here are three popular influencer marketing tools: Hootsuite Hootsuite is a social media management tool that allows you to manage your social media accounts and track your influencer marketing campaigns. Collabstr Collabstr is an influencer marketing platform that connects brands with influencers. It allows you to search for influencers based on their niche, location, and engagement rate. Insense Insense is an influencer marketing platform that uses AI to match brands with influencers. It allows you to create campaigns, track results, and manage payments. Key takeaways Finding and working with influencers can be an effective way for small businesses to reach their target audience. Before you start looking for influencers, it's essential to determine your goals and identify your target audience. You should also understand the legal rules and regulations around influencer marketing, and make sure the influencer is relevant to your brand. Ready to start with influencer marketing even as a small business? Keep reading: How to work with influencers even without a budget Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) How much should I pay influencers? Determining influencer rates can vary greatly depending on factors such as follower count, engagement rate, and the influencer's niche. Some influencers may work on a flat fee basis, while others prefer a commission or a combination of both. It's important to negotiate fair compensation that aligns with your budget and the influencer's value. Should I work with micro-influencers or macro-influencers? Both micro-influencers (influencers with a smaller following) and macro-influencers (influencers with a larger following) have their advantages. Micro-influencers often have higher engagement rates and a more niche audience, making them effective for targeted campaigns. On the other hand, macro-influencers have a wider reach and can provide more visibility for your brand. Consider your goals and budget to determine which type of influencer is the best fit for your small business. How do I measure the success of an influencer campaign? To measure the success of an influencer campaign, track key metrics such as website traffic, sales, engagement, and follower growth. Compare these metrics to your campaign goals and evaluate the return on investment (ROI). Additionally, monitor qualitative aspects such as brand sentiment and audience feedback to gauge the overall impact of the campaign. Can I collaborate with influencers even with a limited budget? Yes, even with a limited budget , small businesses can still collaborate with influencers. Consider partnering with micro-influencers who may offer more affordable rates or be open to product exchanges. Focus on building authentic relationships and offering value to the influencer and their audience. How do I find influencers in a specific niche? To find influencers in a specific niche, you can use influencer marketing platforms, social media hashtags, or conduct manual research. Look for individuals who consistently create content related to your niche and have an engaged following. Additionally, explore industry-specific forums, groups, and communities where influencers may be active. Can I approach influencers directly without using a platform? Yes, you can approach influencers directly without using a platform. Platforms can streamline the process, but reaching out to influencers directly allows for a more personalized approach. Start by engaging with their content, establishing a connection, and then send a well-crafted message explaining why a partnership would be mutually beneficial.

title: Dari Pelajar Aliran Sains Tulen ke Duta Pandai: Kenali Aqil Zulkiflee
summary: Aqil Zulkiflee Duta Pandai — dari pelajar aliran sains tulen ke duta pendidikan. Kenali kisahnya yang menjadi inspirasi buat pelajar SPM.
body_text: Keluarga Pandai baru je dapat ahli baharu! Aqil Zulkiflee secara rasmi menyertai kami sebagai Duta Pandai — dan kami tak sabar nak kongsikan kenapa journey akademik beliau jadi inspirasi untuk ribuan pelajar SPM di luar sana. Jom kenali Aqil dengan lebih dekat. Aqil Zulkiflee dilahirkan di Hospital Besar Melaka , dan perjalanan akademiknya konsisten sejak bangku sekolah: Tadika PASTI (umur 5–6 tahun) Sekolah Kebangsaan Semabok (7–12 tahun) — UPSR 2A 3B Sekolah Menengah Jenis Kebangsaan (SMJK) Yok Bin (13–17 tahun) — PMR 5A 3B, SPM Aliran Sains Tulen 5A 2B 2C Matrikulasi Tangkak , Aliran Sains Tulen Modul 1 — CGPA 3.3 (18–19 tahun) Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) , Sains Kesihatan (Persekitaran & Pekerjaan) — CGPA 3.4 (20–23 tahun) Dengan latar pendidikan dalam aliran sains tulen sehingga ke peringkat ijazah di USM, jelas bahawa Aqil sendiri ialah seorang yang benar-benar menghargai nilai pendidikan. Ikuti laman media sosial Aqil di: Instagram (@aqilzulkiflee) TikTok (@aqilzulkiflee) YouTube (Aqil Zulkiflee) Facebook (Aqil Zulkiflee) Buat Aqil, peluang ini ialah satu impian. Beliau berkongsi hasrat untuk memastikan pengikut dan mereka yang mengenalinya turut menjadi insan yang terpelajar dan terdidik, satu matlamat yang menjadikan kerjasama ini terasa begitu serasi. Mungkin ada yang tertanya-tanya — kenapa Aqil? Jom kita kongsikan sebab di sebalik pemilihan ini. Kenapa Pandai Memilih Aqil Zulkiflee Sebagai Duta Pandai Dekat di hati pelajar dan dipercayai. Aqil mempunyai pengaruh yang kuat dalam kalangan pelajar dan generasi muda — dan yang lebih bermakna, tahap kepercayaan yang tinggi dalam kalangan pengikutnya. Kepercayaan inilah yang membolehkan mesej pendidikan sampai dengan lebih berkesan. Personaliti positif dengan gaya yang santai. Sebagai contoh yang baik kepada remaja, gaya penyampaian Aqil yang santai dan mesra menjadikannya mudah didekati. Mesej pembelajaran pun terasa lebih relevan dan dekat untuk generasi digital. Serasi dengan misi Pandai. Kolaborasi ini dibina atas keserasian nilai (brand fit), bukan semata-mata populariti. Aqil selari dengan misi Pandai untuk menjadikan pembelajaran lebih menyeronokkan dan mudah diakses oleh semua. Kandungan yang benar-benar berkesan. Setiap kandungan bersama Aqil konsisten dengan capaian dan engagement yang tinggi — masing-masing telah mencapai lebih 100,000 tontonan di pelbagai platform. Lebih membanggakan, ia bukan sekadar menaikkan kesedaran, malah menggalakkan lebih ramai pelajar benar-benar menggunakan Pandai untuk belajar. Ini Baru Permulaan Pandai tidak memilih Aqil semata-mata kerana beliau terkenal. Pandai memilih Aqil kerana beliau mampu membantu lebih ramai pelajar melihat bahawa belajar boleh menjadi menyeronokkan, relevan, dan dekat dengan kehidupan mereka. Dan ini baru permulaan. Nantikan lebih banyak perkongsian menarik bersama Aqil Zulkiflee, Duta Pandai!

title: How to Prevent Change Orders on Lump Sum Projects: An Estimator's Guide
summary: Scope gaps cause disputes averaging $60.1M on major projects. Learn the pre-bid habits that keep change orders off lump sum contracts in 2026.
body_text: TL;DR Lump sum contracts shift all scope risk to the GC — every gap comes out of your margin. Scope gaps are caused by specific, repeatable habits — not bad luck. They can be prevented. "Errors and omissions in contract documents" has been the #1 construction dispute cause for 6 of the last 9 years (Arcadis, 2025). The fix starts at bid time: drawings-first review, specific document references, and trade-by-trade scope tailoring. The eight habits in this guide reflect patterns from 200+ GC interviews — the firms with the best margins do these consistently. Why Lump Sum Change Orders Hurt More Than You Think On a lump sum project, the contract price is fixed. Every scope gap that surfaces after award becomes a negotiation — or a loss. There's no cost-plus buffer. No shared risk with the owner. Just your margin absorbing whatever the documents didn't cover. The 2025 Arcadis Global Construction Disputes Report puts the average U.S. construction dispute value at $60.1 million. Most of those disputes trace back to one root cause: "errors and omissions in contract documents." That category has ranked #1 for 6 of the last 9 years. This isn't a design problem. It's a pre-construction problem — and estimators are the last line of defense before it becomes expensive. The Real Source of Most Scope Gaps Scope gaps are not random. They follow predictable patterns. FMI's Construction Disconnected report estimates that $31 billion in rework happens annually in the U.S. — 26% from communication breakdowns, 22% from bad project data. Almost all of it traces to decisions made (or not made) in pre-construction. The gaps that cost the most tend to come from three places: Vague scope language — "as per plans and specs" is not a scope. It's a dispute waiting to happen. Drawing conflicts — civil and structural show one thing, architectural shows another. Neither trade coordinator flags it until field installation. Assumed inclusions — items that feel "obviously included" until the sub sends a clarification letter at buyout. A $45K stone-depth mismatch between civil/structural and architectural drawings on a single slab. A $300K lead-lined glass scope absorbed by the GC under "readily inferable" language. A $400K roof cover board missed on a $50M project, recovered only through a relational favor from the sub. These aren't freak events — they're documented examples from real GC pre-construction teams. For a deeper look at how scope gaps form and compound, the Scope Gap Playbook — built from 200+ GC interviews — is the most thorough resource available. Eight Habits That Keep Change Orders Off Lump Sum Projects The best-margin GCs aren't smarter. They're more consistent. These eight habits come from the firms that have figured out how to prevent scope gaps before bid day — not discover them during buyout. 1. Drawings First, Not Boilerplate First Start every bid review by reading the drawings — not your company's standard scope template. Templates reflect the last job, not this one. The drawings tell you what's actually being built. Treat them as the primary source of truth, and use your template as a checklist against them. 2. Specific Document References, Not Generic Incorporation Scope sheets that say "as per plans and specs" are the single most-cited anti-pattern in GC pre-construction. It sounds complete. It isn't. Every trade-specific scope item should reference the exact drawing number, specification section, or addendum that governs it. If you can't point to a document, the item isn't defined. As one Pre-Construction Lead at a Top-ENR Canadian GC put it: "It's descriptive — bread, put it on a plate, use the open jar… You have to get to that level of detail or else they'll just be like, 'you didn't tell us that.'" 3. Front-Load Buyout Conversations Subs are reading the same documents you are — and they're drawing their own lines around scope. The gap between what you assumed they included and what they actually priced is widest at bid time and narrowest if you talk before the bid is due. A Pre-Construction Lead at a Top-ENR Canadian GC said it plainly: "If you miss anything, they'll bill it." Front-loading buyout conversations doesn't slow down bidding — it eliminates the worst surprises at award. 4. Templates as a Floor, Not a Ceiling Standard scope templates exist to ensure you don't miss the obvious. They are not a substitute for reading the project documents. Every job has something unique — a specialty system, a phased occupancy requirement, a site constraint. The template won't catch it. Your review of the actual documents will. 5. The Pre-Bid Walk Is a Scoping Tool Most estimators treat the pre-bid walk as a courtesy. The firms that prevent scope gaps treat it as a scoping exercise. What are the actual site conditions? What does the demo scope really include? Where are the access constraints that don't show up on drawings? The walk is your only chance to see what the documents don't show. 6. Sub-Specific Tailoring — Sophistication Matters A $10M mechanical sub and a $200K specialty subcontractor are not the same counterparty. Scope communication that works with a sophisticated MEP firm may leave gaps with a smaller trade contractor who won't ask questions they should have asked. Tailor scope detail to the sophistication level of who's receiving it. As an Estimating Manager at a Canadian ICI GC observed: "We have less subs who just kind of a gentleman's agreement… they've become more quick to clarify that we're not including that one piece of scope." That's not a sub problem. It's a market condition. Write scope accordingly. 7. Clarifications, Not Just Exclusions Exclusion lists protect you legally. Clarification lists protect you operationally. When scope is ambiguous, don't just exclude — clarify what you've priced. "Excavation included to 1.5m below grade; deeper excavation by change order if encountered" is more defensible than "excludes unforeseen conditions." 8. The Pre-Issue Scope Review Checkpoint Before any scope package goes to a sub, it should pass through one structured review. Not a five-minute skim before bid day — a deliberate check against the current drawings and specs. One person, one hour, one checklist. This is the habit that catches the $400K roof cover board before it becomes a post-award argument. The Anti-Patterns That Create Change Orders The eight habits above prevent scope gaps. The patterns below create them. If any of these sound familiar, they're worth addressing as a team. Anti-Pattern Why It Fails "As per plans and specs." Undefined scope = disputed scope at buyout. Copy-paste from the previous similar job Scope from Job A doesn't fit Job B. Gaps form in the delta. Junior estimators stuffing previous scopes verbatim No one has reviewed the current documents. Everything is assumed. PMs drafting contract terms inside scope sheets Two people now own scope language. Neither is accountable. Generic "inferred scope" laundry lists Broad language invites disputes over what "general conditions" covers. The five-minutes-before-bid review Nothing gets caught. Everything gets assumed. "Just send the bid docs." Subs price what they see. Gaps in the docs become gaps in the bid. Trade-Specific Gaps That Appear Most Often on Lump Sum Bids Certain trades generate scope gaps more reliably than others. If your lump sum bid involves any of the following, pay close attention to these specific items. For a full breakdown by trade, see the Trade-Specific Scope Gaps chapter of the Scope Gap Playbook. Site and Earthwork Geotech compaction requirements not shown on drawings The five-foot transition between civil and building drawings — who owns it? Excavator unit-rate exploitation when soil conditions differ from the bore log Concrete Grouting base plates — almost never explicitly assigned Slab assembly conflicts between structural and architectural drawings Concrete pumping — included or extra? MEP Generator field conditioning costs — recurring dispute on lump sum hospital and institutional work Motor starters: specified in electrical, priced by mechanical? Fire-rated louvres — in envelope, mechanical, or fire-stopping? Lighting controls — often scattered across electrical and low-voltage specs Envelope and Roofing Roof cover board — frequently omitted from the roofing scope despite being spec-required Masonry-to-storefront flashings — who owns the transition? Fire-stopping at envelope penetrations — excluded by default by most subs Specialty Curtainwall mock-up costs — often not included by the curtainwall sub Lead-lined glass in imaging suites — a $300K omission absorbed by the GC in one documented case Mass timber material protection — no clause, no obligation The Disconnect Between Pre-Con and the Field One pattern shows up in almost every GC interview: scope packages written in pre-construction don't survive intact into project management. A Director of Pre-Construction at a Mid-Market Southeast GC described it this way: "Pre-con is working in the scope sheet world and project management is working in the scopes of work." These are different documents. When the translation happens at handoff — if it happens at all — scope detail gets lost. The PM inherits a contract, not a scope. The sub's understanding of what's included drifts from the estimator's. The fix isn't more documentation. It's better-structured scope packages that survive the handoff without interpretation. That means specific document references, trade-tailored language, and scope items written clearly enough that the PM and the sub read the same thing. A Senior PM at a Toronto mid-market developer said it simply: "If we could catch three scope gaps or three missed items on every scope of work, then this thing pays for itself." How AI Can Help — When It's Built for This Manual scope review takes 30–40 hours per bid. On competitive lump sum pursuits, that time pressure is where gaps get missed. Estimators run out of hours, not thoroughness. Provision's Scope Agent generates complete scope-of-work packages from construction documents in under 60 minutes. It reads the full project set — drawings, specs, addenda — and produces trade-specific scope packages with document references built in. It's not a template filler. It reads what's actually in the documents and flags what's missing or conflicting. For contract and specification risk review, Risk Review runs a structured checklist against your documents with 99.5% accuracy on pre-built risk items. It surfaces the "readily inferable" language, the missing material protection clauses, and the ambiguous inclusions — before they become change orders. When you need to find a specific clause across a 2,000-page project manual in under 20 seconds, Chat Agent answers directly with citations. No more hunting through spec sections on bid day. Provision has reviewed $100 billion in project value and processed 66,000 documents. The patterns it flags are the same ones that appear in the operator examples above — because they come from the same source: real GC pre-construction work. See how EllisDon used Provision to save $1.8M on a single project — and how Cleveland Construction uses it to move through pursuits twice as fast. Where to Start You don't need to overhaul your entire pre-construction process. Start with the habits that create the most risk on lump sum bids: Eliminate "as per plans and specs" from every scope package you issue. Add a pre-issue scope review checkpoint before any package goes to a sub. Front-load buyout conversations on the trade scopes most likely to generate gaps: MEP, envelope, specialty. Review the Scope Gap Playbook with your estimating team — the trade-specific gap list alone is worth the read. If you're running more bids than your team can fully review, look at Scope Agent — it's built for exactly that constraint. Change orders on lump sum projects are mostly preventable. Not by working harder — by building the right habits into your pre-construction process and using tools that read documents the way your best estimator does. Frequently Asked Questions What causes most change orders on lump sum construction contracts? "Errors and omissions in contract documents" has been the top cause of U.S. construction disputes for 6 of the last 9 years, according to Arcadis. In practice, this means vague scope language, drawing conflicts between trades, and items assumed included by the GC but excluded by the sub. How does scope gap prevention differ on lump sum vs. cost-plus contracts? On cost-plus, unforeseen scope costs are shared with the owner. On lump sum, the GC absorbs them. That makes scope gap prevention a margin issue, not just a paperwork issue. Every gap that surfaces after award is a direct hit to your bottom line. What is "readily inferable" language and why does it matter on lump sum bids? "Readily inferable" contract clauses require the GC to include anything that a reasonable contractor should have anticipated — even if it's not explicitly shown in the documents. A $300K lead-lined glass scope was absorbed by one GC under this language. Review every lump sum contract for this clause and price accordingly. Which trades generate the most scope gaps on lump sum projects? MEP, envelope, and specialty trades generate the most recurring gaps. Generator field conditioning, roof cover board, curtainwall mock-ups, and fire-stopping at penetrations are the highest-frequency items. The trade-specific chapter of the Scope Gap Playbook covers these in detail by trade. How long does a proper scope review take on a complex lump sum bid? Manual scope review for a complex commercial lump sum project takes 30–40 hours per bid. Tools like Scope Agent reduce that to under 60 minutes by reading the full document set — drawings, specs, and addenda — and generating trade-specific scope packages with document references included. What's the difference between an exclusion list and a clarification in a scope package? An exclusion list tells the owner what you're not doing. A clarification tells them exactly what you priced and how. Clarifications are more defensible in a dispute because they define the scope positively. Use both — but don't rely on exclusions alone to protect your lump sum position. Can AI actually help prevent change orders, or is it just marketing? Purpose-built tools can. Provision's Risk Review achieves 99.5% accuracy on pre-built risk checklists across real construction documents. Scope Agent reads the full project set and flags missing items, drawing conflicts, and incomplete spec callouts. Generic AI tools like ChatGPT lack the construction context and structured output that estimators need for this work.

title: RTX's Pratt & Whitney Canada to invest $275 million CAD in Longueuil facility, with support from the Canadian and Quebec governments
summary: Funding will enhance capabilities at Pratt & Whitney Canada's global headquarters and largest manufacturing site LONDON, July 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Airshow — Pratt & Whitney Canada announced today a $275 million Canadian dollar investment to enhance manufacturing operations at its Longueuil, Quebec, facility. The investment will be funded by Pratt & Whitney Canada with support from Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada and the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec. Pratt & Whitney is an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business.
body_text: RTX's Pratt & Whitney Canada to invest $275 million CAD in Longueuil facility, with support from the Canadian and Quebec governments July 21, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email Funding will enhance capabilities at Pratt & Whitney Canada's global headquarters and largest manufacturing site LONDON , July 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Farnborough International Airshow — Pratt & Whitney Canada announced today a $275 million Canadian dollar investment to enhance manufacturing operations at its Longueuil, Quebec, facility. Pratt & Whitney is an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business. "This strategic investment in Longueuil strengthens our industrial capacity, enabling us to better support our customers and meet growing global demand," said Satheeshkumar Kumarasingam, president, Pratt & Whitney Canada. "It also reinforces our longstanding role as a pillar of the Québec aerospace ecosystem and a major contributor to Canadian aviation." With this investment, Pratt & Whitney Canada will enhance industrial capabilities at its largest manufacturing facility, where nearly 4,500 employees support the production of engines for regional, business, general aviation and rotorcraft platforms. The site will add automated production lines, modernized machinery and cutting-edge digital processes, helping to drive greater efficiency and precision throughout its operations. About Pratt & Whitney Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business, is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power units for military, commercial and civil aviation customers. Since 1925, our engineers have pioneered the development of revolutionary aircraft propulsion technologies, and today we support more than 90,000 in-service engines through our global network of maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
